title: axis — one (configuration, axis) constraint from S3 (4.5.2)

caller_id.description:
<qid>:v<N>:<config>:<axis>, issued by the fan-out launcher, never chosen by the sub-agent (4.3.1). The revision is part of the id because the id is also the server's isolation unit: without it the same axis at two revisions shares one session context, and a re-run inherits the attempt it exists to replace. Revision 1 writes v1 rather than omitting it -- an implicit default is the shape that has already caught five rules here. The form without v<N> is accepted while the cards that predate a6dca6a migrate, and stops being accepted after.

Optional since 2026-09-22 (3c4629f, §5). It does two jobs -- naming which caller asked the store, and pinning the session context an axis is isolated in -- and an axis that asks the store NOTHING has neither: no caller to name, no query to isolate. Requiring it there forced a card to name a caller that never called, and the three ways out were all closed by contract rather than by effort: emptying `degraded` makes check 45 demand a log line for a caller_id that never called; dropping `caller_id` was refused here; dropping `degraded` reads as empty through `or []`. So the falsehood grew three per revision and stood at twelve axis cards carrying a caller beside a non-empty `degraded`.

Check 45 was already written for this case -- `if not cid: continue` -- so the case was possible in the checker and impossible in the schema, and the schema is what was wrong. The precedent was already in the repository too: a `goal` card carries no caller_id, carries `degraded: []` and honest `kb_refs`, and check 45 skips it. Measured by `simulation-2`, ruled by architecture, and the reading that the fix belongs in the schema rather than the check is the librarian seat's.

kb_version.description: pinned by S3.0; every sibling cites the same one (check 33)

method.description: deterministic output takes computed: sources, an estimate takes assumed: (4.5.2)

inequalities.description: One entry per inequality this axis owns, derived from 4.5.3 rather than declared here. It exists because `abstain_reason` is one string and an axis owns several inequalities: folding seven verdicts into one sentence makes prose, and prose is what 4.5.2.1 replaced. The failure it prevents is specific -- an axis that says nothing about two of its five inequalities reads as 'this axis does not constrain there', and S4 cannot tell that from 'this axis could not compute'. An interval with neither min nor max is not a way around it; that is the silence itself.

missing.description: Named inputs that were absent. Required when kind is no_input: naming them is the difference between a gap someone can close and a shrug.

then.$comment: Exactly one of the three. A returned bound must say something, and what it says comes in three shapes: a numeric range, a discrete set of permitted values, or a requirement on the plan. oneOf and not anyOf because two of them on one inequality is two bounds wearing one entry, and S4 would intersect the pair it recognised and drop the other.

counterexample.description: required when verdict is infeasible: which value exceeds which limit (P5)
